question.worked_solution:
The domain of $y=\sqrt[6]{x}$ is

$$
x\ge 0.
$$

To find the domain of $t(x)=-5\sqrt[6]{6x+3}-8,$ we replace $x$ with $6x+3$ in the above inequality. This gives

$$
6x+3\ge 0.
$$

Solving this inequality, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}6x+3 & \ge 0 \\ 6x & \ge -3 \\ x & \ge -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of $y=t(x)$ is $x\in [-\frac{1}{2},\infty )\,.$

We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of $y=t(x)$ is shown below.
